facts.statement: The genus Stromerosuchus was established by Oskar Kuhn in 1936.
The species Stromerosuchus aegyptiacus was named by Oskar Kuhn in 1936.
Stromerosuchus is a dubious genus of crocodyliform that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: Stromerosuchus (meaning "Ernst Stromer's crocodile") is a dubious genus of Late Cretaceous crocodyliform.

facts.statement: Fossil remains of Stromerosuchus have been found in the Cenomanian-age Bahariya Formation of Egypt.
facts.quote: Fragmentary remains have been found from the Cenomanian-age Bahariya Formation of Egypt.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Stromerosuchus was collected by Ernst Stromer and Richard Markgraf in 1911.
facts.quote: The holotype was collected by Ernst Stromer and Richard Markgraf in 1911

facts.statement: The fossils collected by Stromer were badly crushed during shipment from Egypt to Germany.
facts.quote: but they were badly crushed in shipment from Egypt.

facts.statement: Due to the poor quality of known remains, the genus Stromerosuchus is currently considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: Because the known remains are so poor, the genus is now regarded as a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Some material previously assigned to Stromerosuchus has been reclassified into the genera Aegyptosuchus and Stomatosuchus.
facts.quote: Some material has been referred to the genera Aegyptosuchus and Stomatosuchus, both named by Stromer from the Bahariya material.

facts.statement: The classification of Stromerosuchus has shifted over time, moving from Crocodylia to Stromerosuchidae, then to Aegyptosuchidae, and finally to Crocodyliformes.
facts.quote: It was assigned first to Crocodylia by Kuhn (1964) and then to Stromerosuchidae by Kuhn (1966) before being moved into Aegyptosuchidae by Molnar (1989) and later Crocodyliformes.

facts.statement: Stromerosuchus lived between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)
